utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stein.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I've asked to address the Court to report on the progress we made during the course of the week relative to our reading assignment, if you will. Before you is exactly what we had to analyse over the course of the week. We've done it in a way that we hope would be helpful to the Court relative to our position. On the top of the cart, you'll find the international armed conflict data that we were asked to analyse. We have forwarded to the Prosecution our position and are prepared to give it to the Court in a summary fashion now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stein, there's a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would it not be convenient to deal with him first, rather than these administrative matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there anything pressing about this which we can't deal with at the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: The only reason I raise it now - frankly, we've done a lot of work to try to make everyone's job simpler - is last Friday, a week ago Friday, the 4th, we were given a new batting list. This past Friday, we were again given a new batting order of witnesses, and, indeed, I've tracked those witnesses, and if Your Honour please, basically what I want to say to the Court, and if I can pass these up you can see the charges that were made in the Prosecution's list. The original list that was to be called is set out on the first page. By a letter dated 4 February, that list was modified. I informed the Prosecution by letter that we would do our best to be ready for all the witnesses that were on our list but we couldn't promise. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: [redacted] This morning at 9.20, we received a summary for the witness who apparently is about to be called. As I told the Prosecution, it may be a situation where we are ready or are not ready to cross-examine, given the changes that have been going on and what we've been doing. Additionally and finally, and I don't want to whine about this, but we got two new binders in our locker today. We haven't had a chance to analyse them or look at them. I said a week ago Friday, "Enough is enough." We diverted our entire staff this week to taking care of this project, we have not been spending time this week preparing our case, and I can be more specific when the Court has time for the administrative matters. I think you'll find our work edifying and, in some ways, made the matters simpler and perhaps created difficulties in others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. As far as the witnesses are concerned, you're in a position, are you, to deal with the first witness? I don't know who that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Well, if you look through these documents, you won't know either, but I'm given to understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's also seeking protective measures, so it's witness number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: On which list, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On any of the lists, in fact. Witness number 1 -- not on the first list. It's Witness number 1 on the second list and thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I don't think it's number 1. I don't know what list Mr. Nice is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witnesses expected to testify according to the letter of the 4th of February. Witness for this week, Witness number 1, the one immediately before Christopher Beese.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Then who will testify next?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Witness next available is number 6. Mr. Lopez-Terres has prepared or is in the process of finally preparing that Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It is hoped that number 2 may be available today. He's not going to take very long in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: His evidence is very restricted --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It has been, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- by order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then we come to Witness number 3. Now, all the changes are determined by or caused by availabilities and refusals and changes of position and so on. As to other witnesses for tomorrow, there is either one or two others. I'll find out the names of those and the order in which they fit in on this list. I have to say that apart from absence, the Prosecution's team has also been affected by ill-health and injury this week - not mine, somebody else's - and, therefore, people haven't always been here who might have been. So for today, we've got 1, 6, and I hope 2, and then 3 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: May it please the Court. We have no witness summary for Witness 1. We have a witness summary for Witness 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness 1 doesn't need a summary. The statement was taken effectively in summary form. It's in 19 numbered paragraphs and it doesn't need further summarising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let's get on with this. Now, I see that the Defence have produced the exhibit for us; is that right? That's all the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I must say, speaking personally, I have some sympathy with the complaints of the Defence about this. Can I be assured, can the Court be assured, that we have now got all the material which you wish to produce before it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So far as I know, the material has been produced. A lot of it, you will find it has been proved on earlier occasions and has been reproduced. It has to be produced on an inclusive basis, and I was hoping we could deal with that this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will deal with it this afternoon. And I think the time has come when enough is enough. Yes, let's have the Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, may we move the cart away?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, move the cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before the Witness comes in, and probably safer in private session, may I make an oral application on his behalf for protective measures. In addition to other problems, on my return yesterday morning, my computer system was down, and I wasn't able to get into it, and still have not. However, I was able to see the Witness number 1 on the list. And the Court will remember, I think, dealing with his potential evidence, and will know the particular issue to which it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the Witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been granted protection by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been granted protection by the Chamber, and therefore your name will not be revealed and your face will not be revealed either. Bearing that in mind, will you look at this piece of paper, which the Usher will bring you, and just say "yes" if it be the case that that is your name on the piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will be known throughout your evidence as Witness AE. Witness AE, were you for a time in the early 1990s, or the early to mid-1990s, a member of the reconnaissance sabotage squadron of the 333rd Mountain Brigade of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start; approximately when did you finish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: On the 1st of January, 1993, I joined, and I left in April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning, who was the Commander of that Brigade, or that Squadron?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The Commander was Dzevad Mekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then later, who became Commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Ekrem Alihodzic [phoen] later. And then after that, Mirsad Sesic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January, 1993, who had control of Busovaca, after a certain time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from approximately what date did they have control of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: From when the war started in Bosnia, when they took control of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that date, were you able to pass through Busovaca in uniform or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, after a while?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, can you remember at all the date after which it was not possible to pass through Busovaca in uniform, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The 15th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a checkpoint established at Kacuni on the road between Busovaca and Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: You mean Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom was that checkpoint manned, in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The BiH Military Police controlled the road from Kacuni to Silovac [phoen], the barracks there, and the Kacuni, Busovaca, Kiseljak, at Kacuni near the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform checkpoint duties there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on duty on the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was there on duty on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: There was the leader, Miralem Delija, Nedzad Karaula, Suad Koluh, and Hamdija Katjaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you stopped vehicles, in general, what inquiries did you make of the vehicle occupants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We asked for papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Military booklets, if they were in uniform. If they were civilians, identity cards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in contact by field telephone or other means with any other Commanders of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sort of people, if any, did you have particular interest at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We checked everyone, and particularly people in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that afternoon, was there an incident involving several vehicles that were travelling in a line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Incident?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was there a stopping of several vehicles that arrived together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day, if you can help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many vehicles were travelling together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you received any advance notice of the arrival of these vehicles or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in the first car, or the first vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: In the first vehicle there was Grubesic. I can't recall his first name --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: -- I don't know it, and his driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this particular Grubesic? What role did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: He was the Commander of the Jokers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that first vehicle a car or a military vehicle, or can't you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second vehicle, what sort of vehicle was it? Who was in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The second vehicle was a jeep, that's how we call it. There was the driver in it, Dario Kordic, Vlado Cosic, and someone else was there. I don't know whom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The third vehicle, can you say what sort of vehicle it was and anything about its occupants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was a civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anything -- can you tell us anything about the occupants, the number of occupants, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: There were three in the fourth vehicle but I did not know any one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fourth vehicle, what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: A civilian vehicle, an Ascona. I know that particular vehicle. There were -- Zeljo Vukadinovic, Dragan Vukadinovic, and Spomenko Akrap were in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know which units any one of those were a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. In the fourth vehicle, we are talking about the fourth vehicle, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They belonged to the Jokers Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any emblems identifying units worn by any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I did not see it there at the checkpoint but I did see it before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you tell us what relation the two Vukadinovics were, one to another, Dragan to Zeljo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Cousins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which vehicle did those of you controlling the checkpoint first approach?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was done? What was asked of the occupants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem Delija and I approached and Miralem asked them to show their documents, their military booklets, and the driver did not give that. He offered his I.D. but Miralem wouldn't take it, he wanted to see the military booklet. Grubesic then began to verbally abuse Miralem, to provoke him, and then we raised our weapons and Miralem approached from Grubesic's side and took away his pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Grubesic dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he provoked, can you give any detail of the provocation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, "Who are you to ask for that?" and other things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened so far as the second car was concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: When we took -- or, rather, when Miralem seized that pistol, and at that moment Nedzad Karaula told Miralem, "Here is your neighbour in the second car," and Kordic was about to get out of the second car, and he said, "Why did Miralem take that weapon?" and he said that he'd pay for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did Kordic go in getting out of the car? Did he get out of the car or did he stay in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, he did not get out of the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How clearly did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Very clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How near to or far from him were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, four metres, could have been four or five metres, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the attitude of Miralem to Kordic when he said, "You'll pay for this," or "You'll pay for that"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Oh, well, Miralem simply laughed. Well, I mean, not laughed as if he was happy to hear that but sort of a cold laugh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Miralem approached Kordic in any way himself or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen that approach?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: He did not come right up to him. He was perhaps a metre or two away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything aggressive in the manner of Miralem's approach to Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. When we stopped the vehicle, Suad Koluh called the Brigade Commander, because we had a field telephone connection, to inform that we'd stopped four vehicles, and we were then notified to let them go and we let them go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever taken a weapon from a vehicle before? I don't mean you personally. Had the people operating the checkpoint ever taken a weapon from a vehicle before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I myself did not do it but weapons were taken; that is, we took them from them and they took it from us in Busovaca and elsewhere, and they were exchanged two or three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular weapon, how would you describe it, if you can now remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We called it a TT, nickel plated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it kept or returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We kept it, that is Miralem kept it, and then he lost it some four or five days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later that day, just yes or no to this, did you discuss events with Delija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Before or after?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards, did you discuss the position of his family, in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. Miralem, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss the Delija family at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: That, yes. Afterwards we wanted to go and get Miralem Delija's family out, to go across the hill to rescue them, because Miralem said they were in peril there. But there were very few of us, only around eight. There were just too few and we did not go to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report for duty the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I got up to go on duty, and I was told then that Mirsad Delija, that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about that first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Ernest Koluh, the Battalion Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Miralem that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, right after that. As Ernest told me, I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you also about the killing of his brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirsad, also known as what? What was his other name, or nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Soco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I come to paragraph 16, the Chamber will discover that there's an error in a name on 16, which is explained by the nickname. And the way to deal with that is to cross refer back to the nickname. It will become clearer if one looks at paragraph 10. It's the nickname that is right and the other name that is wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AE, were you at the checkpoint some days later when you saw something of one of the men who had been in the four cars that had been stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: January 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using not the full family name, but the nickname, which was the man you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Charlie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just remind us, paragraph 10, what's the full name of Charlie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Spomenko Akrap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I knew him very well, because we were school fellows, and we were together in the drama section. We spent there many years together, and we went -- we attended the same elementary school at Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what vehicle was he travelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was a jeep, a relatively small one, and it had "police" written on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, I think, of the group to which Charlie, Spomenko Akrap, belonged. He was, was he, one of the Jokers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Driving a vehicle marked "police," was there anything unusual in that or not, for a member of the Jokers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which direction was he travelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: From Busovaca to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stop him and detain him, or let him through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I did stop him, but I did not arrest him. I let him through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he had passed, was Miralem around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me whom had I stopped, and I told him that I had stopped Charlie. And he asked me, "Why did you let him go?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. If you look at the paragraph 16, you will see we are into the range of unreliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, it's the comment of Miralem, who has since died.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Correct. And the basis of his knowledge is unclear, and so we could be talking about second, third, fourth reports, or rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a question of weight, isn't it? Like many of these hearsay points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Of course. It's also a question of prejudicial versus probative and how you balance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll admit this evidence. Clearly, as against the man Charlie, it would not be evidence on which a great deal of reliance could be placed. But as part of the evidence in the case, it's admissible. What weight it will have, will depend on how it fits in, if at all, with any other evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that Miralem --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that Miralem said about Charlie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: To Charlie or about Charlie?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About Charlie.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: All he said was, "Why did you let him go?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: "He killed my Soco."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had been discussing the previous day the possibility of the Delija family moving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? Which part of the Delija family were you referring to? Was it Miralem's family, was it Mirsad's, was it the parents, or who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Parents and a brother, I think. Miralem Delija's wife was in Zenica already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where Miralem lived at that time, and whether he lived with his parents, or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem had his own house, but it was nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where his brother, the one who was killed, was living at the time or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I believe he was living with his parents, but I'm not a hundred per cent sure. But I do think that he lived with his parents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the stopping of Charlie, and Miralem saying what he did, did an armoured vehicle appear at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: First UNPROFOR came, rather their vehicle, and they wanted to go the route and move on towards the barracks, towards the silo, but our order was not to let them through towards the barracks. So we lined up and would not let them; that is, we turned the weapons at them and did not let UNPROFOR through. And they lined around the meadow, around the mosque and beyond the mosque. And as we were there with UNPROFOR, an HVO vehicle arrived with a PAM, and an anti-aircraft machine gun was there. And it opened fire on us, and on people who were in the meadow. And our people responded and the armoured vehicle went through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after Charlie's passage did this armoured vehicle arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Some 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody injured in this burst of firing, or the response to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now, please, look at the one exhibit that I'd ask you to deal with, Z410.2. And the English version can go on the ELMO, the witness having the original version. This is a document dated the 27th of January, apparently over the name of Pasko Ljubicic, and it relates to something that happened on the 24th, and something that happened on the 25th. As to the 24th, it speaks of fire opened from infantry weapons on the Kiseljak-Busovaca road, and it speaks of somebody being killed, together with a civilian person who had been driving. So that would be two people being killed. And it says that fire was opened by Muslim forces, both persons were massacred and stabbed with knives. Were you present on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right that two people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: When the armoured vehicle arrived, a Toyota car came up. Ivica Petrovic was driving it. He was in a military uniform and he also opened fire on us. And one of our members fired a Zolja at the car, and Ivica Petrovic was killed on that occasion. And there was another civilian with him. I know him. Now, I don't know whether this was a nickname or a proper first name, but we called him Srecko, and he escaped from the car. And our man took him over to the other side, that is to the Croat side. In other words, he stayed alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The account of the -- this is not for the witness, it's just for the Chamber's benefit. The account of the two persons relates to another exhibit that the Chamber was dealing with a couple of weeks ago. I am not going to deal with paragraph 19, having discussed the matter with the Witness. It seems to fall on the wrong side of the remoteness test that the Chamber applies. Thank you. You will be asked some further questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Witness AE, allow me to introduce myself. I am lawyer Mitko Naumovski from Zagreb, one of the Defence counsel representing Dario Kordic. I have several questions for you, but in view of the interpretation into the official languages of the Court, please wait a few seconds before giving us your answer. Witness AE, you made a statement to the investigators, or, rather, one of the Prosecutors on the 16th of December, 1999. I assume you remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever before made a statement to anybody whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over a period of seven years since this incident, which occurred in January 1993, until the 16th of December, 1993, did you discuss this event with anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't remember. I may have done. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember at all. Officially or privately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Perhaps I spoke privately about it, with a member of the family or someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, Witness AE, you told us exactly when you were a member of the BH Army. Tell us, before the 1st of January, 1993, did you belong to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the period from May or June 1992 until the end of 1992. Were you in the TO in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: From April 1992, I was in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: In Lugovi and then later in Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Lugovi organisationally came under the Busovaca TO, didn't they? The Commander was Husein Hadzimejlic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, Witness AE, that after the HVO took control in Busovaca in May 1992, the TO continued its activities with its headquarters in Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: For a time, the headquarters were in Lugovi, as I said. Afterwards it moved to Kacuni. I don't know the exact date, when the TO moved to Kacuni, but it did go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we agree that the TO was operating in the territory of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, in the territory of the municipality but not in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we also agree - I assume you know this because many of your colleagues were living in the town of Busovaca - that they travelled to work in Kacuni from Busovaca in that period of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question related to January 1993. You said that from the 15th of January, 1993, there was a prohibition on the carrying of weapons and uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and do you agree with me that this was a joint command, a joint order issued by Colonel Blaskic and the Commander of the 3rd Corps, Hadzihasanovic, that people should not carry weapons and uniforms in inhabited areas, that this was jointly decided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let us now focus on the events of January 1993. If I understood you well, you were a member of a Reconnaissance Sabotage Squad of the 333rd Brigade. You said today that control on the road was held by the Military Police, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: You mean Kacuni? In Kacuni and the road towards the barracks, that's the road going from the mosque to the barracks, and this was controlled by the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The answer is not in the transcript, when you agreed with me that you were a member of the Reconnaissance Sabotage Squad of the 333rd Mountain Brigade. Your answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Military Police controlled this road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Not the main road but the road going from Kacuni to Kasina, which is a road branching off from the main road, and the IDV held a checkpoint on the Busovaca-Kiseljak road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So members of this Reconnaissance Sabotage Squad manned this checkpoint in Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether this checkpoint was manned by members of a Company of the 2nd Battalion under the command of Sead Sljivar. What was your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, the checkpoint at Kacuni, on the main road from Busovaca to Kiseljak, was not held by the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we agree then that the Reconnaissance Sabotage Squad had some special assignments related to that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: They were not special assignments; we simply manned the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us briefly what your duties were at the checkpoint, to stop all vehicles and check personal documents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that, checking documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know. It was our duty to examine them and take note of them in a logbook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you recorded the names of all the persons whose documents you had checked, you took their names down in a book.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When exactly was that checkpoint established, with the continuous duty of examining vehicles and passengers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness said in his evidence the 15th of January. That's what he said so there's no need to ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I didn't hear that. Then I can move on and accept that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we do agree, Witness AE, that Croats were mostly moving along this road through Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, mostly, in the direction of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we also agree that members of the HVO were persons of special interest for you whom you needed to check?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today that on the field telephone you received orders regarding certain particular vehicles. Who gave you those orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't get orders to search vehicles, but those we considered to be interesting, we searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I read that from your statement, under point 5 when it says, "Sometimes we received orders over the field telephone to search certain vehicles of interest to us."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: When we reported that we had stopped someone in uniform, I said that sometimes we confiscated the weapons. I personally didn't but others did seize weapons from some HVO members, so it's quite possible that we also searched them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is who was the person who gave you approval or orders to do that, your Commander or someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: As far as we were concerned, my squad, Miralem made the decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go on to this event that you say occurred on the 20th [Realtime transcript read in error "23rd"] of January, 1993. My first question is, do you know which day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know. Please speak up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you listed the names of the persons who were with you at the checkpoint. My question is was Semir Jugovic from Kacuni with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. Semir Jugovic was a member of the Military Police. He was not with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that there were several dozen soldiers at the checkpoint and around it on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, I'm sorry to interrupt but you put the 23rd of January. I thought the evidence was it was the 20th. I'll be corrected if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be either my mistake or a mistake in the translation. I was referring to the events of the 20th of January. This is a mistake. I'm sorry. The 20th of January, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, from which direction did you check vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Vehicles coming from both directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This checkpoint was established using old tyres and other means to block traffic. Both lanes were not free.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Both lanes were open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't use any special obstacles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How, then, did you stop vehicles, by raising your hand, simply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, alongside the road was a large truck parked with logs, loaded with logs, parked at right angles with the road, outside the carriageway.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us refer to the weapons that you had, you members of this reconnaissance sabotage squad. What kind of weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We had automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean automatic rifles? What model were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: They were manufactured by Crvena Zastava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also have pistols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone have a so-called RPG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We had that in the little house, the little hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean, please, "in the hut"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Where the field telephone was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had an RPG ready. Several pieces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, one. We didn't have that much weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone in particular in charge of the use of that RPG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We all knew how to handle it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was listening carefully to you but I didn't hear you tell us from what direction these vehicles had come.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Kiseljak-Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mean from Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether they were coming from Kiseljak, but from that direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, could you please describe to us how those vehicles approached. Were there other vehicles on the road, UNPROFOR trucks, or any other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these vehicles approaching? What was the distance between the individual vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: They were close. I really couldn't say how many metres separated one from the other. Three, four, five metres, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you today when this was and you said it was in the afternoon. Could you be perhaps more precise? Was it about 5, later, or before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was earlier; it wasn't just before dusk. So it could have been between 12 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's what you consider the afternoon. This was January. Was it cloudy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember? Let me put it differently. Had it become dark already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few words now about these approaching vehicles. For the first vehicle, you said that Grubesic was in it in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't really know him, this Grubesic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him at the time either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem Delija knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As he was in civilian clothes, how did you know that he was the Jokers Commander when you didn't know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem knew that and the others who knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But who told you? You don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, let me say Miralem told me. Somebody told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So somebody told you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to give you the name, would that remind you of the person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. I don't know that person, I never knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must tell you, Witness AE, that your testimony today differs from what you said a month or so ago. You said explicitly that both Grubesic and the driver in the first vehicle were in uniform. This is item 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The driver was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "In the first car was Grubesic in a camouflage uniform. With him was a driver also in a camouflage uniform."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The driver was in a camouflage uniform, I said that, but as for Grubesic, I don't believe I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you speak up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The driver was in a camouflage uniform. That's why we asked him to show his military booklet. And the person, the gentleman sitting next to him, I don't think that is what I said. But I read it out to you. That is what it said here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't agree with what I read out, that Grubesic was in a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that vehicle that arrived first, you and Miralem Delija approached it. Who conducted the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem Delija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we agree that you approached the vehicle with your guns pointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. We pointed the guns at the vehicle when Grubesic started insulting Miralem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please explain how you held your weapons before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: On our shoulders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your shoulders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the driver obeyed immediately, and he gave you his personal ID card. This is a means of identifying people; is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. For us he was a soldier, and he had to have a military booklet. And on that booklet, not only his name, but also the unit he belonged to had to be indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that that was what you were going to say. So one of your tasks was also to establish the deployment of troops passing through your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When Miralem Delija pointed his gun at Grubesic, he also opened the door of his car, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to see that the persons in the car had weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Delija still insisted that weapons be handed over to him, if there were any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Grubesic did so? He gave up his pistol, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that Delija lost that pistol later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: We were together that day when he lost it, and we went looking for it and we couldn't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after the event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Four or five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your duties at the checkpoint was not to seize private weapons, but to keep it, put it away somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Miralem kept that weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he did so without the necessary authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. He had the right to keep the weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't have to hand it over to his command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, his command knew that he had taken the weapon, and he didn't hand it over to the command. It is normal for a leader to have a pistol, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know, Witness AE, that later on a request was made to return that pistol of Grubesic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I heard those stories. There was a rumour that I think Kostroman demanded that the pistol be returned, but these were just stories. It's something I just heard, as a rumour. However, I think that that is not true, that no request was made to restore the pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned Mr. Kostroman, do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I know from stories that he was the President of the municipality in Busovaca. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness AE, let us go onto the second vehicle now. Tell me, please, do you know anything in particular about that jeep, the brand, the colour, the registration plates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I can't remember what kind of registration plates there were at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't give us any further detailed description of that vehicle, at least the colour? Well, if you don't know, tell us you don't know. That's an answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how many persons were there in that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Four persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the person, whom you recognised as Mr. Kordic, sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: He was sitting in front, next to the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the passengers dressed in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: In civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All four of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe any detail about the clothing worn by Mr. Kordic? Was he wearing a suit, did he have a tie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't remember any detail regarding his clothing? Did he have a coat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, he must have had a coat. It was wintertime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but, please, don't make any inferences. Did you see him wearing a coat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. No. I really don't remember anything, those details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did he have a hat on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the length of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: He was -- he had a short cut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did he have a beard, or a beard and a moustache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing glasses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that this second vehicle was approached by Nedzad Karaula. Where was he from? Is he from Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: He is from Bukovci. It's a village in Busovaca municipality near Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he called Miralem Delija, how far away from you was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: About -- he was three or four metres away from the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That must have been the distance. Since you were next to the first car, the second car was behind the first car, so you were looking at it from the front. And Miralem Delija made a couple of steps towards that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not? You stayed next to the first vehicle, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, Witness AE, you said that the person whom you identified as Mr. Kordic was about to leave the car, and then he addressed a couple of words to Miralem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that he objected to why the weapon was being taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: "Why are you doing that?" He said, "You will pay for this." That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AE, when you made your statement less than two months ago, you said that Mr. Kordic opened the door of the car and called out something to Miralem. You didn't actually cite the words you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I always gave these words. I heard those words being spoken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing I can do is to show the Witness his testimony in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let him see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at point 12, please. And will you read out what has been highlighted. Do you agree that that is what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first part, that he called out something; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is nothing as to what was said, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "no"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this afternoon, for the first time, you are telling us that something was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, this is not a fair way of putting it. Look at the paragraph and, so that the record is clear, I will read the English translation: "At this point Kordic opened the car door and called out something to Miralem. Miralem approached Kordic. Kordic then threatened Miralem, saying, 'You will pay me for this.' Miralem laughed at him." And that is what paragraph 12 of the statement has.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I quite agree with you. That is precisely my question. If the Witness didn't hear the first words that were called out, I wanted to ask how come he managed to hear the other words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It doesn't say here that I didn't hear them. It says that he called something out to Miralem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, Witness AE, but "something" means that you don't know what, otherwise the words would have been taken down. But it is, of course, up to Their Honours to judge. What was the tone used by Mr. Kordic, when he uttered the words you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: So that it could be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a shout or was it in a normal voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, he didn't shout, but the answer was a sharply intoned one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miralem Delija was approaching Kordic just then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also agree that he still had his automatic rifle in his hand, and that automatic rifle was pointed forwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. He held his automatic rifle in one hand, pointing downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, after those words that you claim were uttered, that Miralem laughed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you told us today that Miralem Delija, towards the end of the day, several hours later, expressed fear for his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come that he should have said that several hours later, whereas here he laughed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. I just explained that a moment ago. Maybe you didn't hear me properly. It wasn't a laugh, as if he was glad that he heard this. Miralem was a taciturn man, and a highly -- a man in control. He didn't wish to react to that provocation. But it isn't true that he was concerned several hours later. He was probably concerned immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said in your statement later on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Later on that day we spoke about this. We discussed the problem of Miralem's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Very well. As for the third vehicle, you also said that it was a civilian vehicle and you didn't recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who approached that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No one approached it. No one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not? It was your duty to check the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Because we received orders to let them go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, this telephone conversation was conducted by one of your colleagues. Did he tell you whom he spoke to? Was it with Husein Hadzimejlic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Husein Hadzimejlic was not the Commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't speak to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clear up this particular detail regarding the passengers of the fourth vehicle. Between the statement you made in writing earlier on, and now, the nickname Charlie is being used for two different people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: That's a technical error. I know Charlie personally. We went to school together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, according to you, Charlie is Spomenko Akrap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, it's now time for an adjournment. Have you very much more for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not more than 15 or 20 minutes, Your Honour. Not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, we'll adjourn. But since you have been dealing with the incident at the checkpoint, I want to be clear about this. Is there any dispute that Mr. Kordic said, "You will pay for this"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in absolute dispute. We are not claiming, but the fact is that Mr. Kordic wasn't at that checkpoint then at all. So it's a completely -- it's a complete mistake of identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you had better put that, then, to the Witness, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me finish. You must put it to the Witness, so he has the chance of answering the suggestion. You must put to him that he's mistaken about Kordic being there at all. Put it to him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AE, you have heard what I told Their Honours. Mr. Kordic was not there at the checkpoint then, Mr. Kostroman and his bodyguards were stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And not only that, they weren't coming from Kiseljak, they were coming from Busovaca going to Kiseljak? The direction is wrong.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know what you are saying. This is what I saw. I know Mr. Kordic, I knew him then, and I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you agree with me that you also knew, because these were well-known persons, and you saw them on television, both Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kostroman and Anto Valenta, and I don't know who else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Blaskic at the time at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'd never seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I did after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Something else is incorrect, Witness AE. I have spoken to many people who have knowledge about this. They are all claiming that this occurred on the 21st of January, or perhaps the 22nd, but on the 21st of January. That is why I asked you whether you knew which day in the week it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know which day in the week, but I know it was the 20th. I wouldn't know if it was the 20th either, if I didn't know that Cosic was killed on the 21st. He was killed that night, actually, and we learnt about that the next day, the 21st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are positive that it was not on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If that's a convenient moment, we'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the break, I put to the Witness our idea as to what happened on that particular occasion, but I forgot about one detail and, if I may, I should like to go back to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AE, can we resume where I put to you the discrepancies between your claims and ours. Just one thing. You said that Mr. Kordic was sitting in the co-driver's place, but Mr. Kordic never said in the front, he was always in the back, he was always in the rear seat. So are you quite sure he was in the front seat, next to the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on. We are still talking about this incident which happened on the 20th of January, 1993. You will agree with me that you told the investigator that subsequently you heard that Blaskic and Kostroman were in other vehicles there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, I said there were rumours to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not recognise them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I did not because I did not know those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you told us that the first person who told you that Miralem Delija's brother had been killed was your Battalion Commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. No, he was not my Commander. He was a Battalion Commander and we were from the 333rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But I didn't remember his name. What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Ernest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he told you about that a day later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise. How did you work during those days, I mean, about shifts? Let's begin with the 20th of January, 1993. Which shift were you on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I worked from morning to nightfall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was during daytime. And the next day, the 21st?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And onward?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is how you worked the whole week until the beginning of the conflict, all the days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: There was no checkpoint at the beginning of the conflict. I don't know whether it was the 25th, but there was no checkpoint. It could have been the 23rd or something like that when we left the checkpoint, but we were there side by side with the Military Police, and the Military Police was right side by side with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't understand. What does that mean, that your reconnaissance sabotage platoon kept that point only for two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Two days or perhaps five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after five days, you were joined by the Military Police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, or, rather, we joined the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So on the 24th of January, 1993, who manned the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The police -- no, nobody. On the 24th, nobody was there on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you told us about what you knew about the events of the 24th of January, 1993, when you say that Ivica Petrovic was killed. Do you know what day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I don't, not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you described to us how he was killed. Were you an eyewitness to that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: You mean, did I see that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you watch directly what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away were you, and where did the fire take place, the gunfire take place, exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you had positions by the side of the road, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. We were on the right-hand side as you walked -- as you face Busovaca, in the meadow, several of us, and several of us were at the checkpoint where, as I said, UNPROFOR was trying to pass through and go to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us about the 24th or the 25th of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The 24th or the 25th, when the conflict broke out. The 25th, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But I'm asking you to be more accurate. Will you please think about it, because I want to discuss two events with you. One of them happened on the 24th and you're telling us that the second one took place on the 25th. So will you please think about it. We're now talking about the incident when Ivica Petrovic got killed, and that happened on the 24th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around three -- twenty minutes past three in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the incident that I'm interested in. Were you an eyewitness to that particular incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you well that there were no more roadblocks on that road, does that mean that Petrovic opened fire out of the blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then somebody fired a Zolja, a hand-held launcher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was another civilian and you said it was one Srecko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that he was released and survived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, he was not released. He simply escaped from the car and then our men escorted him to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are claiming that he left the scene of the event alive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with Ivica Petrovic, Igor Bogdanovic was also killed in that same place during that critical incident?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not get the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you sure about that? Your Honour, you see that we disagree with the witness, and we shall also prove that Igor Bogdanovic was killed on that same occasion, and I can put it to the witness once again, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, I think we can go on. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then let us move onto the next day, to the 25th. You said that incident took place when UNPROFOR vehicles were involved. And you said, on the 25th of January, 1993, you blocked the passage to UNPROFOR vehicles which wanted to go to the barracks at this silo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what time was it, or what part of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was after 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Busovaca and in that area, had the conflict already begun by that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, the conflict broke out that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But that day in the morning, early in the morning, on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: In Kacuni it broke out on the 25th, when the armoured vehicle came up to Kacuni and opened fire on us, and that is when we started firing and that is when the front lines were established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your statement, item 16, you said, "On the 25th of January, 1993, I was at the checkpoint when the conflict in Busovaca broke out." And then you describe how you intercepted Charlie. From this I conclude that a conflict in Busovaca had already begun.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Listen, the conflict in Busovaca never really started. There was no conflict in Busovaca. They merely disarmed people. And that is what happened there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, how many men were there at the checkpoint when UNPROFOR vehicles were stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know. There were quite a number of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quite a number. I see. And you used your weapons to stop the vehicle from moving on to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, first without weapons. I mean, we had weapons over our shoulders, but they wanted to go through, and then we were issued the order to stop them by hook or by crook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is when you used weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, but we never fired them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you did not fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stopped that Charlie, or whatever his nickname was, and let him through without ever stopping them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did you let him through if, first, you saw him in the vehicle on the 20th, and meanwhile you had already heard that Miralem Delija's brother had been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't really know why, and I am still sorry that I let him through. I'm still sorry today that I let him through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you today, before the break, that is I mentioned the name of several persons who were public figures, who appeared on television, so on and so forth, and you told us that before January you had never seen Blaskic on television, and Kostroman, that you also never saw him on television before that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, not to this day. Kostroman, I don't know Kostroman to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never watched those press conferences that were transmitted, that were broadcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the only person that you knew was Mr. Kordic, you told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: [Nod]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: From the media. And I knew him well. I just knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him as what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Only by following the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean you were not politically active; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: [Nod]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer was "yes," wasn't it? I said: You were not politically active, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we are coming to the end, and this could be my last question. Will you tell us, please, you said that today that you were writing the vehicles and names of persons in a book that you kept at the checkpoint, and then this book of record was turned over to the Commander of your reconnaissance unit or to the commander of the 333rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
